fields.apa_citation: Grêt-Regamey, A., & Galleguillos-Torres, M. (2022). Global urban homogenization and the loss of emotions. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-27141-7
fields.main_conclusion: Homogenized peri-urban residential landscapes trigger weaker physiological (skin conductance) and self-reported (SAM valence/arousal) emotional responses than urban or rural landscapes, and unlike in urban and rural areas, emotional responses do not significantly predict people's place-making intentions in peri-urban areas, implicating lower social cohesion and place attachment there.
independent_variables: Landscape/scene type (urban vs. peri-urban vs. rural residential VR scene)
fields.construct_pair: Landscape homogenization (urban vs. peri-urban vs. rural exposure) -> Emotional/physiological arousal and place-making engagement
fields.stimulus_description: Participants wore a VR headset with integrated earphones and viewed 2D 360° photographs (with matched ambisonic soundscapes) of an urban, a peri-urban, or a rural residential street scene from either Switzerland or the Netherlands, each shown for two minutes.
fields.methods_surface_summary: 285 adults recruited on the street via a mobile VR lab in two countries were exposed, in randomized order, to urban, peri-urban and rural 360° VR scenes while skin conductance was recorded continuously; after each scene they rated valence/arousal (SAM), and afterward completed a questionnaire on place attachment, social cohesion and place-making, analyzed with Friedman tests, a Generalized Linear Mixed Model, and stepwise/AIC-based regression.
measurement_inventory: Skin conductance / electrodermal activity (phasic and tonic components, Ledalab decomposition)
Place attachment questionnaire (based on Bonaiuto et al., 2015)

notes.apa_citation: Title, authors, and DOI (10.1038/s41598-022-27141-7, an s41598 prefix = Scientific Reports) are printed in the text ('© The Author(s) 2022'), so year is set to 2022; however no volume/issue/page numbers are printed anywhere in this extraction, so the reference is incomplete on those elements.
notes.direction: IV is a 3-level categorical landscape type rather than a continuous/binary variable, so 'positive/negative' is approximate: peri-urban exposure (relative to urban/rural) is associated with lower/blunted (i.e. more negative-valence, lower-arousal) physiological and self-reported emotional responses, hence coded 'negative'.
notes.p_value: Multiple significant p-values are reported for the physiological-response comparison (Friedman tests): phasic slope angle p=6.1e-3, phasic AUC p=3e-4, tonic AUC p=1.1e-2. p=3e-4 (phasic area-under-curve) was chosen as representative of the headline physiological finding (peri-urban < urban/rural); other p-values for the same overall claim are given in the source text.
notes.effect_size: No canonical effect-size statistic (d, r, eta2) is printed for the main peri-urban-vs-other comparison; the closest quantities are the Friedman chi-square statistics (e.g. chi2(2)=16.4) and the regression R2-adjusted values by scene type in Table 1 (rural 0.49, urban 0.22, peri-urban 0.13), neither of which is a direct effect size for the main IV->DV contrast, so left null.
notes.sample_n: 285 total participants exposed to the VR scenes (Methods, Participants); subsequent regression analyses used smaller, place-specific sub-samples (33-113) after listwise deletion for incomplete survey answers.
